page: Amazon Web Services r8idb.large is an entry-tier instance within the memory-optimized r8idb family, powered by the AWS Nitro System. Hardware resources include 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with two threads on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor capable of reaching 3.9 GHz. It features 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The processor integrates advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, AMX int8, AMX tile, and SHA-NI, paired with a massive 480 MB L3 cache. Accelerated local storage is directly integrated, providing a 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture optimized primarily for single-threaded processing and memory capacity rather than parallel throughput. The instance achieves strong scores in single-core Geekbench (2152.0) and single-threaded compression tests, including 33.79 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.37 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics reflect the physical single-core ceiling, showing weak performance in multi-core Geekbench (2707.0) and stress-ng multi-core testing. PassMark database operations and large-block uncached memory read bandwidth also sit in lower percentiles, while static web serving throughput posts an average 7.34 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency for the r8idb.large stems from its tight integration of DDR5 RAM and bundled local NVMe storage without requiring external block storage charges for scratch disks. However, workloads requiring intensive parallel compute, sustained multi-core compilation, or large-model machine learning inference will encounter severe throughput constraints due to the two-vCPU count. The instance is best suited for lightweight in-memory caching nodes, small Redis instances, intermediate data processing with local caching requirements, and memory-sensitive services requiring strong single-thread efficiency.
description: Amazon Web Services r8idb.large is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical Intel Xeon 6975P-C core operating at 3.9 GHz, 16.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, and a 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume. Advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX are supported on the x86_64 architecture. Performance evaluations show strong single-threaded throughput, particularly in single-core Geekbench and compression tasks, contrasted with weaker multi-threaded scalability constrained by the two-vCPU ceiling. With 2 Gbps baseline networking and a generous 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the instance provides cost-effective efficiency for low-scale memory-bound workloads, such as distributed cache replicas, localized staging databases, and single-threaded data batch jobs.
